_meta.description: Suburban-SOC unified security index. Pins ECS fields to keyword/ip/date so cross-index aggregations and dashboards are consistent (fixes the dynamic text+keyword drift that silently failed shard aggregations). WS0.3: tenant.id is a first-class keyword. WS0.5: backed by a per-tenant data stream (logstash-security-<tenant>) under ILM policy logstash-security-ilm. #249/#250: command-line/script-block-shaped fields (process.args, *CommandLine, *ScriptBlockText, *uri — explicit properties plus the long_command_fields dynamic_template) use a lowercase normalizer (so Sigma's lowercase literals match mixed-case real telemetry via wildcard-query normalization) and a raised ignore_above so long values, e.g. encoded PowerShell, aren't silently dropped from the index. #263: process.args/process.parent.args/winlog.event_data.ScriptBlockText/winlog.event_data.ImagePath (and the long_command_fields dynamic_template backing any future field of the same shape) are raised further to ignore_above:32766 — 8191 (#249/#250's original raise from the default 1024) was still below real PowerShell 4104 chunk sizes (~20000 chars) and encoded-command-line lengths, letting both PowerShell Sigma rules and system_win_suspicious_service_binpath_lolbin.yml be silently bypassed by payload length. Note ignore_above:32766 is a CHARACTER ceiling, not the Lucene per-term 32766-BYTE hard limit it's numerically equal to — multi-byte UTF-8 content can exceed the byte limit while under the char ceiling, which would otherwise reject the whole document rather than just dropping the field (confirmed live during #263's review); configs/logstash.conf's ruby filter clamps byte-oversized values before they reach Elasticsearch to prevent that, tagging pipeline.byte_clamped separately from pipeline.truncated. Aggregations/sorts on these fields return the lowercased form; _source keeps original casing for Discover/evidence (except the rare byte-clamped case, where _source itself is clamped too — no way to preserve full fidelity there without risking the same document-rejection failure). #290: the 5 new Zeek-derived ECS fields #228 introduced never got long_command_fields' lowercase_normalizer/raised-ignore_above treatment, falling through to strings_as_keyword (case-sensitive, ignore_above:1024) instead — tests/detections/sigma_eval.py matches case-insensitively by default (mirroring real Sigma semantics) but production Elasticsearch does not for an unnormalized keyword field, so a single uppercase char anywhere in real telemetry silently evades net_zeek_dns_crypto_mining_pool.yml/net_zeek_dns_doh_non_standard.yml (query|endswith) and net_zeek_http_cobalt_strike_beacon.yml (uri|contains) while the fixture test stays green. Fixed with explicit properties (dns.question.name, tls.validation_status, zeek.http.host, url.path) rather than extending long_command_fields' path_match glob — path_match matches the FULL dotted path, so the existing `*uri`/`*url` patterns never actually matched `url.path` (the path doesn't END in "url"), which is exactly why it silently fell through despite looking covered; explicit properties sidestep that ambiguity entirely and match this file's own established convention for every other case-normalized field. url.path alone gets ignore_above:32766 (not 8191, unlike its 3 siblings) — it had NO explicit ignore_above at all before this fix (falling to the default 1024), confirming #290's own suspicion that the uri->url.path rename (#228) silently dropped ignore_above coverage; 32766 matches the payload-length intent the pre-existing `*uri`/`*url` long_command_fields patterns were meant to provide (C2 beacon URIs/exfil query strings, same bypass shape #263 fixed for PowerShell). user_agent.original (also named in #290) deliberately excluded: unlike the other 4, no producer renames or maps it anywhere in this pipeline today (suburban-soc-ecs.yml's own comment: field mapping "deliberately omitted... no rule selects on it yet") — normalizing a field nothing populates would be speculative, not a real fix; whoever adds it later must ALSO rename configs/logstash.conf's Category 0 bare user_agent string to user_agent.original in the same commit, or Zeek http.log's unrenamed string collides with the object mapping and drops every zeek.http document (same collision class already handled for zeek/version/the :5514 user_agent path). Security-auditor follow-up review of this same fix found and closed 2 more gaps: url.path's new ignore_above:32766 was not added to configs/logstash.conf's #263 byte-clamp long_fields hash, live-confirmed to reintroduce whole-document Lucene immense-term rejection on a fully attacker-controlled field (HTTP URI) — fixed by adding it there, plus a new CI-enforced CeilingConsistencyTests check that WALKS this template for every field at ignore_above:32766 and asserts each has a matching clamp entry, so a future field raised to this ceiling cannot skip it silently. And tls.client.server_name — same #228 batch, same case-sensitive hostname shape, with both a producer (configs/logstash.conf) and a live dashboard consumer (network_dashboard_v3.ndjson's SNI panel) — got the identical lowercase_normalizer/ignore_above:8191 treatment as its tls.validation_status sibling. ignore_above:8191 (used for every field here except url.path) is not an arbitrary convention: 8191×4=32764 is the largest character ceiling that stays under Lucene's 32766-BYTE hard limit for arbitrary UTF-8 even after lowercase_normalizer's case-folding growth (a handful of code points, e.g. U+0130, grow when case-folded) — 32766 requires the logstash.conf byte-clamp entry above; 8191 does not. OPERATIONAL NOTE: this is a data-stream-backed index template (see data_stream above) — like every prior ignore_above/normalizer change to this file (#249/#250, #263), it only shapes indices created AFTER it is applied; an operator must roll over each logstash-security-<tenant> data stream (POST <data-stream-name>/_rollover) for it to take effect on the currently-active write index, the same manual step #263 documented performing against the running production stack. #292: dns.answers (the new TXT-record-download-direction field) got an explicit ignore_above:8191 property rather than falling to strings_as_keyword's default 1024 — security-auditor review: unlike dns.question.name, which a 253-byte DNS-name protocol limit makes structurally unable to reach even the DEFAULT 1024 ceiling, a Zeek dns.log answers array element has no such bound, so the field this fix's own net_zeek_dns_txt_answer_abuse.yml rule selects on could be silently unindexed past 1024 chars — a query that can never find the value, not a crash, and with no pipeline.truncated tag either (dns.answers is deliberately NOT in configs/logstash.conf's long_fields byte-clamp hash, matching every other 8191-ceiling field here). Deliberately NO lowercase_normalizer: the rule's own answers|re pattern already spans both cases in its character class, so normalizing would only cost case-folding byte growth for no matching benefit. WARNING for a future raise to ignore_above:32766: configs/logstash.conf's byte-clamp ruby filter only clamps String values (`next unless val.is_a?(String)`) — dns.answers is a Zeek Array, so a long_fields entry for it would satisfy CeilingConsistencyTests' CI gate while the clamp itself silently no-ops, reintroducing the #263 whole-document rejection bug with CI green. Do not raise past 8191 without first making the clamp array-aware. #288: percent_lost/gaps/acks/ts_delta (Zeek capture_loss.log, bare unrenamed field names, no configs/logstash.conf entry maps them) got explicit numeric properties for the same reason every other explicit property in this file exists — index.mapping.ignore_malformed is true and the two dynamic_templates below only match_mapping_type:string, so a bare numeric field falls to Elasticsearch's own default dynamic type inference entirely, decided by whichever document happens to create the field first. percent_lost's steady-state healthy value is exactly 0 (an integer-shaped JSON number), so the very first capture_loss doc in a fresh backing index is the SAME shape as a #275-class false-healthy trap: if that first doc pins the field as a long, every later fractional value (3.7, 12.5 — the values scripts/setup/ai_agent/slo_metrics.py's capture_loss_max_pct metric actually needs to see) is silently ignore_malformed-dropped from the index while remaining in _source, so the metric reads a permanent, healthy-looking 0.0 while the sensor is actually dropping packets. Pinned to float explicitly so the type is never left to chance on rollover (data streams re-derive dynamic mappings from the template independently on each new backing index).
